top.title: Petrol, Food Prices Rise Further As Iran War Worsens El Niño Impact Globally — UN
top.description: El Niño disrupts global weather patterns, bringing heavy rain to some regions and drought to others, and spiking food and fuel prices, a situation worsened by the ongoing war in Iran, according to the Chief Economist at the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), Maximo Torero. Speaking with AFP, Torero said both rain and drought can impact harvests and production of crops for animal feed. Floods can be particularly devastating, destroying stored food and damaging the infrastructure and transportation needed to get products to market. All these elements can push up prices, and the impacts “can emerge well before harvests are completed,” he said. “Markets react to expectations of future shortages and uncertainty itself can generate volatility,” he told AFP. This year’s El Niño impacts are exacerbated by price shocks caused by the war in Iran, which have raised the cost of fuel and fertiliser for farmers and impacted household spending globally. “For vulnerable households, even moderate food price increases can have huge consequences,” said Torero. “Poor families spend a large share of their incomes on food and therefore have limited capacity to absorb price shocks and spikes,” he added. The consequences can include reduced food consumption, poorer quality diets and “ultimately, increased food insecurity and malnutrition,” he said. In September, the FAO said it had received just one-fifth of the $202 million it requested to prepare for an El Niño-linked food crisis in 22 high-risk countries. Here is how the climate phenomenon has been playing out around the world in the last week. People walk from a market while balancing their purchased food and household supplies on their heads in Ifotaka, in southern Madagascar, on September 23, 2026. Photo by RAZAFINDRAKOTO MAMY NIRINA / AFP Heat Record The world is on track for 2026 to be the second-hottest year on record, with the El Niño weather pattern turbocharging human-driven global warming, the European Union’s climate monitor said Friday. “October has continued the pattern of remarkable global warmth, with record global and surface ocean temperatures,” said Samantha Burgess, strategic lead for climate at the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, which operates the Copernicus monitor. “An exceptionally strong El Niño is adding further heat to a climate already warmed by human activities,” she said. top.title: ‘Didn’t know much about him’: DeMarcus Cousins says his favourite Lakers player is not Luka Doncic
top.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images Luka Doncic is the biggest star in the Los Angeles Lakers’ locker room. The Slovenian is one of the best in the business, and if he continues at the same rate, he will likely win the MVP award this season. That is why Doncic is almost everybody’s favourite Lakers player, but DeMarcus Cousins’ pick is actually someone else. DeMarcus Cousins says Walker Kessler is his favourite Lakers player Walker Kessler joined the Los Angeles Lakers in July via a sign-and-trade deal on a four-year, $130 million contract. The 25-year-old had made a terrific name for himself while playing for the Utah Jazz, and his game has gone up a level since moving to LA. Kessler usually starts at centre alongside Doncic, and even though it’s the latter who makes all the headlines, the former has mostly been incredible as well. Cousins has watched a lot of the Lakers this season, and he has named Kessler as his favourite player ahead of the likes of Doncic and Austin Reaves. He said on the Run The Ball show: “My favourite player in this team is Walker Kessler. “I didn’t know much about him in Utah, but the way he controls the paint and the way he protects the rim… He had a few incredible blocks against Ausar Thompson, who is a freak athlete.” Cousins then had his say on the Lakers, a team he had made fun of before the start of the season. He has now held his hands up and admitted that they deserve respect. He said: “This is a pretty well-rounded team. Early on, there were a lot of jokes. I was one of the main people joking. It didn’t quite look great on paper. But seeing how this team is starting to shape up, you’ve got to put some respect on this Lakers group and the guys on this team. “Reaves is playing at an All-Star level right now. He put on an incredible performance. I love everything I’m seeing from this Lakers team right now.” The Lakers really are looking good, and everyone on the team, like Kessler, is producing the goods on a consistent basis. That, combined with Doncic playing out of his skin and looking like the next MVP, gives the Los Angeles side a great chance of going all the way this season. top.title: Arsenal have already blown their WSL title chances - but Gunners still have the talent to win another Women's Champions League
top.description: Arsenal UWCL hopes GFX - Getty/GOAL Renee Slegers' side have underwhelmed domestically this season, but as huge games with Barcelona and Lyon approach, opportunity knocks for them to remind everyone they could still be capable of something special in Europe With nine games gone in the Women's Super League season, Arsenal sit sixth in the standings, having gathered just 13 points to sit a massive 12 off the pace of leaders Manchester City. Even at this early stage, their hopes of lifting a first WSL title since 2019 look doomed. Yet, as strange as it may seem given their struggles, that does not mean they should be overlooked in the Champions League. It's not been smooth-sailing in the early knockings of their European adventure by any means. A narrow 1-0 win over HB Koge in their first outing was a real struggle, with the Danes unlucky not to get anything from a game won by Mariona Caldentey's stoppage-time penalty . Then came an eventful 2-2 draw away at Paris FC, where an inexplicable handball by Leah Williamson allowed the hosts to complete their comeback from 2-0 down . At the time, there was a feeling that could be the final game for head coach Renee Slegers. But the Dutchwoman remains at the helm as the Gunners prepare for a huge couple of weeks in this competition having overseen a much more convincing 3-0 win over Benfica in the team's last European outing. Now, two huge tests beckon: away at Barcelona, the reigning champions , on Thursday before the hosting of eight-time winners Lyon a week later. It's a great chance for Arsenal, winners of this competition just 18 months ago , to remind everyone what they are capable of. Slow starters Arsenal have a history of starting seasons slowly, with them still able to come on strong in the latter stages of the previous two campaigns Many will argue that Arsenal don't deserve to be spoken about as Champions League contenders after their start to the season. The Gunners have regularly looked out of ideas, defensively weak and unable to maximise the talent in this squad, which was massively increased by what looked, on paper, like an outstanding transfer window . But it is worth noting that Arsenal have a history of starting seasons slowly. It was that which ultimately cost the Gunners a shot at the WSL title last term, with them only finishing four points behind eventual winners City in the end. Regrets were traced back to September and October, where draws against Manchester United and Aston Villa proved costly before a defeat to City. It meant their subsequent 17-game unbeaten streak in the league was somewhat in vain. A year previous, a run of one win from the opening four league games would spell the end of Jonas Eidevall's time in charge. It was another campaign in which Arsenal were the closest rivals to the eventual WSL champion, but they were nowhere near an invincible Chelsea in the end. top.title: What made Youri Tielemans’ first Man United strike unique in Premier League era
top.description: What made Youri Tielemans’ first Man United strike unique in Premier League era Manchester United’s Youri Tielemans opened his account for the Red Devils at the weekend. Goalscoring The Belgian is not renowned for scoring large numbers of goals, but when he does, they are usually spectacular or important. Or both, as in the Europa League final last season for Aston Villa against Freiburg. Tielemans scored just ten times for his former club in 134 matches. In addition, he added only 28 strikes in 195 games for Leicester City, but one of them was the winning goal in the 2021 FA Cup final. Man United goal Tielemans thought he had opened his account last month against Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford, but the goal was ruled out. Nonetheless, he finally got on the scoresheet during his 14th match for the club, having been an ever-present so far this season. The Belgian midfielder pulled his side level at 2-2 just before half time against Aston Villa when Zion Suzuki could not keep out the effort. His muted celebrations were out of respect for his former team, even though he must have been delighted to open his account in front of the Stretford End in such dramatic circumstances. The club’s official website has also reported on why the goal was special. The site reports, “it’s taken pretty extensive research but, by our reckoning, no United man has ever scored his first Premier League goal for the club against a former side.” Teddy Sheringham also almost did in August 1997 against Tottenham Hotspur, but his penalty cannoned off the post and out. Ralph Milne did achieve this in 1988 when he scored his first United goal against his former side Charlton Athletic. Tommy Boyle also scored in 1929 against his former side Sheffield United, and George Livingston in 1909 against his old team, Manchester City.

What does that mean? MLB is making an attempt for outfielders to play “straight away” in left field, center field, and right field. The idea is to keep outfielders from adjusting their positioning based upon the known hitting tendencies, or from which batter’s box the hitter swings the bat. Specific positioning areas are marked in all three outfield areas. Outfielders must remain in those designated, marked areas until the pitch is thrown, and the ball is hit. In theory, the experimental rule is designed to increase the number of balls hit in outfield gaps. If a player is stationary, in one specific spot, the outfielder will have to adjust quickly to a ball hit to either side of his dictated position. In theory, the experiment is designed to increase the number of hits. Hits of all kinds; singles, doubles and triples. More hits translates to more action. More action translates to more runs scored. top.title: All quiet on extension front as Sal Stewart's value rises with award
top.description: LAS VEGAS – Sal Stewart’s Rookie of the Year award brought good news and bad news for the Cincinnati Reds this week. The good news is that thanks to new rules in the game meant to disincentivize service-time manipulation the Reds get an additional draft pick between the first and second rounds. The not-so-good news: The price just went up on the inevitable extension talks with the hard-hitting, 22-year-old All-Star. Reds GM meetings 4 great free agent fits for Cincinnati Reds as MLB's GM meetings open Four months after the Reds inked Stewart’s pal, Reds ace Chase Burns, to a $105 million, seven-year extension, the Reds and Stewart still had not engaged in talks about an extension for the 32-homer rookie slugger, sources said. And the meter continues to run after Stewart became the franchise’s ninth player to win the National League Rookie of the Year award, with Stewart also a finalist for a prestigious Silver Slugger award. Those winners are announced next week. The tangible upside for the team — beyond possibly earning a few more ticket sales in marketing the “award-winning” Sal — is the Prospect Promotion Incentive draft pick that figures to be a top-40 overall pick between their first- and second-round picks. That’s because of a 2022 rule that rewards teams for promoting prospects closer to the beginning of a season rather than wait long enough with their better prospects to assure an additional year of club control before free agency. That delay of less than two weeks led to players such as Kris Bryant and Maikel Franco to file union grievances a decade ago against their teams for service-time manipulation that delayed their free agency. Bryant won a Rookie of the Year award in 2015 after being kept in the minors the first eight games of that season, which meant an additional six years before he was eligible for free agency. How potentially valuable are the additional supplemental picks? Stewart was selected 32nd overall in 2022 – as an additional compensation pick for the Reds for losing Nick Castellanos as a free agent. nigeria.description: El Niño disrupts global weather patterns, bringing heavy rain to some regions and drought to others, and spiking food and fuel prices, a situation worsened by the ongoing war in Iran, according to the Chief Economist at the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), Maximo Torero. Speaking with AFP, Torero said both rain and drought can impact harvests and production of crops for animal feed. Floods can be particularly devastating, destroying stored food and damaging the infrastructure and transportation needed to get products to market. All these elements can push up prices, and the impacts “can emerge well before harvests are completed,” he said. “Markets react to expectations of future shortages and uncertainty itself can generate volatility,” he told AFP. This year’s El Niño impacts are exacerbated by price shocks caused by the war in Iran, which have raised the cost of fuel and fertiliser for farmers and impacted household spending globally. “For vulnerable households, even moderate food price increases can have huge consequences,” said Torero. “Poor families spend a large share of their incomes on food and therefore have limited capacity to absorb price shocks and spikes,” he added. The consequences can include reduced food consumption, poorer quality diets and “ultimately, increased food insecurity and malnutrition,” he said. In September, the FAO said it had received just one-fifth of the $202 million it requested to prepare for an El Niño-linked food crisis in 22 high-risk countries. nigeria.title: I sold heavy weapons internationally – Orji Kalu
nigeria.description: …Says he sold arms to anyone who could buy The Senator representing Abia North, Orji Kalu, has disclosed that he previously engaged in the international trade of heavy weapons, selling arms to buyers in different countries before quitting the business at the insistence of his parents. Kalu made the revelation during an interview on Arise Television on Monday, while discussing his business background and relationships with former and current South African leaders. Asked whether he was an arms dealer, the former Abia State governor answered in the affirmative, saying he stopped after his parents intervened. “Yes, so I stopped because my parents, my mother, my father came and said I must stop, and I stopped,” he said. Asked whether he sold weapons to people who intended to use them to kill others, Kalu dismissed the suggestion, saying his motivation was to make money. “No, no, no, no, no, no. I was selling guns to make money, whether they blow up it’s not my business,” he said. The interviewer subsequently asked whether he supplied weapons to the African National Congress (ANC) during its struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Kalu said he did not restrict his business to the ANC, explaining that he sold weapons to any buyer who could afford them. “No, I was selling to anybody who wants to buy. If you have the money, you want to buy in D.R.C, I sell to you, you want to buy in Namibia, you want to buy…” he said. Asked about the source of the weapons, the senator declined to provide details, saying, “It’s only my business.” The interviewer also questioned how his former arms trade related to Nigeria’s current security challenges and the proliferation of small arms. In response, Kalu clarified that the weapons he traded were not small arms but heavy weapons sold between countries. “No, these are heavy arms that were sold country to country,” he said. Asked specifically whether he sold weapons to Libya under its late leader, Muammar Gaddafi, Kalu said he sold to anyone with the financial capacity to purchase them. “To anybody that had money to buy,” he responded. nigeria.title: 2027: Most Christians we’ve engaged are okay with Muslim-Muslim ticket – Yilwatda
nigeria.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, says most Christians consulted by the party have expressed satisfaction with the Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Vice President Kashim Shettima ahead of the 2027 general elections. Yilwatda said Christians’ initial concerns that the arrangement could marginalise them had not materialised, insisting that their voices remained represented in the administration. The APC chairman stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday. “Most Christians that we’ve engaged and we’ve spoken to them, they are very okay with the Muslim-Muslim ticket,” he said. “The thought and the fear of most Christians was that the Muslim-Muslim ticket may suppress their voices, but their voices are heard loud and clear now.” He also dismissed concerns that Tinubu’s religion had exposed Christians to discrimination or persecution during his three years in office. On questions surrounding the President’s health and fitness to contest the 2027 election, Yilwatda maintained that Tinubu was physically capable of seeking re-election. He also defended the President’s decision not to attend every campaign rally, arguing that his constitutional responsibilities would not allow him to participate in all party engagements. According to him, some government officials have been advised to attend selected rallies to ensure that governance is not affected by campaign activities. On the leadership crisis rocking the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Yilwatda denied allegations that the APC was behind the party’s internal dispute following the Federal High Court judgment invalidating the David Mark-led leadership. He questioned the opposition party’s decision to blame the ruling party over a dispute arising from a legal action instituted by one of its members. The APC chairman further expressed confidence that Tinubu would defeat former Vice President Atiku Abubakar in a free and fair election. He attributed Atiku’s performance in the 2023 presidential election largely to the political structure of the Peoples Democratic Party rather than his personal popularity. “He did not win because of Atiku; he won because of the structure of the PDP. It was the PDP that brought Atiku, not Atiku winning on his own,” Yilwatda said. He also defended FCT Minister Nyesom Wike’s proposed ₦10m reward for councils that deliver their wards for Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the incentive did not constitute vote buying. nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Chairman of Etsako East Local Government Area of Edo State, Rt. Hon. Ekpeson, who is also the Edo State Chairman of the Association of Local Governments of Nigeria (ALGON), gave the directive during an emergency security meeting with vigilante leaders and coordinators to address security concerns ahead of the festive season. The chairman warned that kidnapping, killings, cult-related activities, violence and other criminal acts would not be tolerated anywhere in the local government area. He also charged security coordinators to strengthen intelligence gathering, improve collaboration among their teams and ensure adequate security coverage across communities throughout the festive period. Those at the meeting included the Vice Chairman, Comrade Charles Aloaye Dagana; Secretary to the Local Government, Dr. Samuel Oshiole Enaboakpe; and Chief Adolphus Oshole Osimi, General Officer Commanding of the Agenebode Zonal Vigilante Command, who oversees security operations across villages in the Weppa-Wanno axis. Other vigilante coordinators also attended the meeting. The statement said Ekpeson reiterated that the protection of lives and property remained a priority of his administration, urging security operatives to remain vigilant, proactive and responsive to distress calls. He further charged vigilante leaders to ensure that the directives translated into concrete action, saying he would not want reports of kidnapping, killings, cult-related violence or other criminal activities across the local government. nigeria.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja The Federal Government has unveiled a N70bn National Oral Health Strategic Plan for 2026–2030 to improve access to dental care, address the burden of oral diseases and eliminate Noma as a public health problem. The five-year plan is designed to expand preventive and curative oral health services, improve early detection and treatment of Noma, strengthen the dental workforce and integrate oral healthcare into primary healthcare services across the 774 local government areas. The Minister of State for Health and Social Welfare, Dr Iziaq Adekunle Salako, announced the initiative on Monday in Abuja during the commemoration of National Noma Day and National Oral Health Day. According to a statement by the ministry’s Assistant Director, Information and Public Relations, Ado Bako, Salako said the initiative aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises the health and wellbeing of Nigerians. Expressing concern over Nigeria’s burden of Noma, particularly in the North-West and North-East, the minister described the disease as preventable but devastating, with the potential to cause severe facial disfigurement, disability and death, especially among malnourished children. He said the World Health Organisation’s recognition of Noma as a Neglected Tropical Disease in 2023 marked a significant milestone in global efforts to combat the condition. Salako disclosed that the Federal Ministry of Health had integrated Noma surveillance into the Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response system, while intensifying efforts to improve early detection and referral through primary healthcare facilities. He added that frontline health workers, traditional healers and traditional birth attendants had been trained in 19 states to identify early signs of Noma and other oral diseases and facilitate prompt referrals for treatment. Highlighting gaps in oral healthcare delivery, the minister said more than 80 per cent of Nigerians had never visited a dentist, while two out of every three children were living with untreated dental caries. One of the things I was particularly looking forward to during my visit to China was seeing the famous Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an. I had read about them, seen pictures and, of course, watched films inspired by the mysteries of ancient China. But nothing quite prepares you for the experience of standing in front of thousands of life-sized soldiers who have been buried underground for more than 2,000 years. And what an experience it was! For anyone who has watched Hollywood’s The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor, you may remember the mysterious army of clay soldiers that comes alive. Well, I finally got to see the real thing. Thankfully, none of them came alive while I was there! But standing in those enormous exhibition halls, surrounded by thousands of soldiers, horses and chariots arranged in military formation, I couldn’t help wondering what must have gone through the minds of the people who created this extraordinary army. The story takes us back to around 221 BC, when Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor to unify China. Like many powerful rulers of his time, he was obsessed with immortality and the idea of continuing his reign beyond death. His solution was to build an entire underground army to protect him in the afterlife. Think about that! While some people prepare for retirement, this emperor was preparing for eternity, complete with his own military formation! The scale of the project is difficult to comprehend. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, horses and chariots were painstakingly created. And what makes the discovery even more fascinating is that the soldiers are not identical. They have different facial features, hairstyles, uniforms and expressions. They look like real individuals, each with a distinct identity and military rank. Then comes another remarkable twist. For over two thousand years, this enormous army remained hidden beneath the earth until 1974, when some local farmers digging a well stumbled upon fragments of what would become one of the greatest archaeological discoveries in modern history. Imagine going out to dig a well and discovering an entire army! I wonder what the conversation was like that evening when they returned home. Today, the site is recognised globally as one of the greatest archaeological treasures in the world and is popularly described as the Eighth Wonder of the World. UNESCO designated the Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor a World Heritage Site in 1987. But beyond the fascinating history, what struck me most was what China has done with this discovery. nigeria.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Oluwo of Iwo, Oba Abdulrosheed Akanbi, has called for the development and promotion of Yoruba language as a medium of instruction for academic subjects, including Physics and other specialised courses. The monarch made the call on Monday during the 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration and his 11th coronation anniversary at his palace in Iwo, Osun State. Oba Akanbi said Yoruba had the capacity to serve as a language of instruction across different academic disciplines if deliberate efforts were made to develop and expand its use. “Normally, I prefer to speak my Yoruba language. I want to upgrade the Yoruba language so that we can use it to teach Physics and all kinds of subjects and courses in the educational system,” he said. The traditional ruler also advocated the preservation and modernisation of Yoruba culture, particularly the reform of traditions he said promoted violence. While praising the richness of Yoruba heritage, he stressed the need to preserve its positive aspects while addressing practices that could encourage violence. “When it comes to culture, I want a culture that is free of violence. I accept all Yoruba cultures and traditions, but those that need modifications, particularly traditions that promote violence, must be addressed. “It is not that I totally reject them, but I understand that change takes time,” he said. The monarch also announced a N5 million empowerment scheme for at least 100 residents of Iwo, with each beneficiary expected to receive N50,000. He said the beneficiaries would be drawn from different segments of the community, including members of the royal institution, princes, chiefs, the Muslim community, traditional initiates and ordinary residents. According to him, beneficiaries will be selected randomly rather than through a predetermined process. The 2026 Odun Olodumare celebration also attracted members of different religious groups to the palace, where they offered prayers and praises to God for the monarch, his subjects, Iwo town and the country. nigeria.title: US-mediated talks with Russia and Ukraine to start in Abu Dhabi
nigeria.description: Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States will hold talks in Abu Dhabi Tuesday on ending Europe’s worst conflict since World War II in the first such meeting in more than nine months, as another winter of war approaches. Europe – alarmed by US President Donald Trump floating a deal with Moscow on European security ahead of the talks – will also send representatives to Abu Dhabi. Trump has pushed for an end to the Russia-Ukraine war since returning to power, but previous talks produced no breakthroughs and the process became sidelined by the US-Israeli war against Iran. Europe and Ukraine fear the United States will force a deal on Kyiv that would amount to a de-facto capitulation, with Trump appearing to pivot towards Moscow this year. Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands, displaced millions and has dragged on for 56 months, with the Kremlin showing no sign of backing down. Trump hinted Ukraine will have to give up land ahead of the talks, saying: “They’re going to end up with a little bit different shape, Ukraine.” Russia occupies large swathes of Ukraine but, while its troops have grinded westwards, they have not been able to seize the whole of the Donetsk region. Moscow demands Kyiv surrender the parts of the region it still controls, vowing it will otherwise press on with its offensive. Ukraine – which for more than 4.5 years has resisted a far larger invading army at a huge human cost – has ruled out such a withdrawal. Russia pummelled Ukraine in the run-up to the talks and carried out one of its deadliest strikes yet – with Kyiv saying 55 people were killed in a frontline village as they queued for humanitarian aid. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the intensified strikes were part of Moscow’s strategy of “putting pressure on Ukraine’s position” at the negotiations. Russia’s Vladimir Putin, who launched the war in February 2022, has repeatedly refused broader ceasefire offers and face-to-face talks with Zelensky. Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner and special envoy Steve Witkoff will gather the enemy sides in Abu Dhabi for the first time since February, when negotiations took place in Geneva. Russia and Ukraine have held several rounds of failed talks during almost five years of war and hopes for peace are low. “We don’t have any particular expectations,” a senior Ukrainian official in Kyiv told AFP. ‘We don’t want Yalta 2.0’ Trump last week floated a “very big agreement” on the war that will “involve all of Europe”, stoking fears Washington would collaborate with Moscow on creating a new European security architecture. Shortly before launching its 2022 invasion, Moscow had issued an ultimatum to the West for NATO to rollback troops from Eastern Europe. nigeria.title: I won’t surrender my senatorial ticket — Uzodimma
nigeria.description: Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State has insisted that he remains in the 2027 Senatorial race, describing suggestions that he would surrender his ambition to another candidate as “a lie”. Read Also: Court sacks Uzodinma as APC senatorial candidate for Imo West A Federal High Court sitting in Abuja, on October 29, 2026, ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to remove Uzodimma’s name as Senatorial candidate for Imo West and replace it with the name of former Governor Rochas Okorocha. Justice Obiora Egwuatu based the judgment on the grounds that Uzodimma did not win the All Progressives Congress, APC, primary election held on May 18. The outcome of the ruling has since been rejected by the APC in the state, with the party insisting that Uzodimma remains its candidate for Imo West Senatorial District. Speaking on Sunday after attending Mass at the Government House Chapel in Owerri, the Imo state capital, Uzodimma dismissed insinuations that he would cede his ticket to anyone as deceptive. “If they tell you that I will hold this ticket and somebody will collect it and give it to another, tell the person it is a lie,” he said. He called on residents of the state to canvass support for the APC to ensure its victory across all levels, mentioning names of candidates voters should rally round in the forthcoming elections. “Go and campaign for the party, our great party, the All Progressives Congress, APC. There is no other political party we are going with. “For the House of Assembly, it is APC. For the House of Representatives, it is APC,” the governor said. He added, “For the Senate, your senator in Okigwe zone is Patrick Ndubueze, in Orlu zone it is my humble self (Hope Uzodimma), and in Owerri zone it is (Alex) Mbata,” he said. Okorocha Meanwhile, Okorocha had earlier described the ruling nullifying Uzodimma’s candidacy as a victory for the nation’s judiciary and democracy. Okorocha, in a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media, Sam Onwuemodo, commended President Bola Tinubu for, according to him, providing the enabling environment for the Judiciary and other Institutions to function for the nation’s rapid development and growth. “This judgment, to say the least, is a resounding victory for the nation’s judiciary. It is a victory for the nation’s fast-growing democracy. It is an outstanding victory for the nation’s Constitution, as amended. He added, “It is a remarkable victory for all lovers of what is right and haters of what is wrong. It is a notable victory for posterity and history. “Finally, it is a victory for Imo people in general, and Imo West Senatorial District people in particular.” Vanguard News The post I won’t surrender my senatorial ticket — Uzodimma appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Explainer: Election results collation chain that decides Nigeria’s president
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – Nigeria’s president is not declared on the strength of a single national count. A chain of collation officers, each signing for the votes below them, builds the result from the polling unit up to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * Why getting most votes is not enough to become Nigeria’s president The chain starts when voting ends. Voters are accredited with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, and the presiding officer counts the ballots in public and enters each party’s score on Form EC8A, the polling unit result sheet. The presiding officer signs the form, and polling agents who are present countersign it. A poster version, Form EC60E, is pasted at the polling unit so voters can see what was recorded. Collation then moves upward. INEC’s then chairman, Mahmood Yakubu, described the 2023 process as running through “four levels”: ward, local government area, LGA, state and national. At each level, an officer adds up the forms from the level below and records the total on a new form. The election results forms The ward collation officer adds up the Form EC8A sheets in the ward and records the total on Form EC8B. The LGA collation officer then adds up the ward sheets on Form EC8C. At state level, the State Collation Officer for the Presidential Election (SCOPE) adds up the LGA results on Form EC8D. Katsina in 2023 shows what that form contains: 3,516,719 registered voters; 1,097,663 accredited; 1,058,673 valid votes, and 32,514 rejected. Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, led with 489,045 votes against 482,283 for Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC. The national stage takes place in Abuja, with the INEC Chairman acting as returning officer for the presidential election. That office is now held by Joash Amupitan, who succeeded Yakubu in October 2025. In 2023, Yakubu set out the procedure at the national collation centre, where each state’s SCOPE presents the original Form EC8D. “When all the SCOPES have presented their results,” the returning officer displays the sealed copies of Form EC8DA, the state-by-state summary, and Form EC8E, the declaration sheet. Polling agents are invited to comment before the winner is declared, and each agent receives duplicate copies afterwards. Declaring winner Declaring the winner involves more than adding up votes. The returning officer must also confirm that the candidate with the highest total reached one-quarter of the votes in enough states, as Section 134 of the Constitution requires. The 2023 totals show the arithmetic. Yakubu put registered voters at 93,469,008; accredited voters at 25,286,616; valid votes at 24,025,940, and rejected votes at 939,278. nigeria.description: By Udeme Akpan, Ediri Ejoh, Obas Esiedesa & Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s electricity generation rose to 4,020.41 megawatts (MW) on Monday from 3,500MW, but the increase has yet to translate into adequate supply for consumers across the country. This comes as the promise last Thursday by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, to restore normalcy in power supply within 72 hours expired two days ago. Data obtained from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 20 power plants were connected to the national grid as of 1.0pm yesterday, producing a combined 4,020.41MW. The output was below Sunday’s peak generation of 4,253.6MW but above the off-peak figure of 3,862.17MW. Last Thursday, generation had dropped to 3,659MW from 3,996MW recorded the previous day, worsening supply conditions across several parts of the country. Promising restoration within 72 hours, the Ministry of Power had ruled out a major or systemic national grid failure, explaining that preliminary assessments linked the disruptions to maintenance and operational challenges across parts of the power value chain, alongside declining generation. An analysis of Monday’s generation profile showed that Afam VI contributed the highest output of 519MW, followed by Shiroro Hydro Power Plant with 445MW and Azura-Edo Independent Power Plant with 438MW. Egbin Power Plant, with an installed capacity of 1,320MW, contributed 108MW. Meanwhile, load allocation to the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) stood at a combined 3,195MW as of 5:07pm yesterday; Abuja DisCo received 581MW; Ikeja 467MW; Eko 458MW and Ibadan 359MW. Others were Port Harcourt, 294MW; Benin, 243MW; Enugu, 233MW; Kano, 173MW; Kaduna, 167MW; Jos, 146MW; and Yola, 74MW. In his update on the power situation, Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, said electricity had been restored to many communities affected by recent disruptions, particularly in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Kwara and the Federal Capital Territory. He disclosed that the vandalised Benin-Egbin 330kV transmission line had been repaired and returned to service, helping to raise electricity supply to the Lagos Complex to more than 1,000MW. However, he acknowledged that some locations were still experiencing outages. “Our priority continues to be the provision of reliable electricity to Nigerians,” he said. nigeria.description: The murder of Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka and his companion, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, on October 26, is an escalation of insecurity. Two gunmen on a motorcycle reportedly opened fire outside the cleric’s residence and fled, leaving both men dead. Ansaru, a jihadist organisation, claimed responsibility in a video, describing Masussuka as an “infidel” and threatening others who reject its interpretation of Islam. Its claim is grave, but investigators must establish who ordered and executed the killings. Masussuka was an Islamic preacher who advocated peaceful coexistence among Nigerians of every faith, opposed violent extremism and owned a Qur’anic television, radio and school. Ansaru reportedly targeted him over his teachings, his criticism of certain Hadith traditions and, most disturbingly, his advocacy of interfaith tolerance. No doctrinal disagreement can licence murder. His assassination is an assault on religious freedom and a threat to moderate Muslims. The pattern belongs to a wider security crisis. In Oyo, abductors killed teacher Michael Oyedokun and circulated footage of his beheading; another Oyo kidnapping case has seen a beheading video admitted in court. Such atrocities, like ransom kidnappings, attacks on rural communities by armed Fulani herdsmen groups and other bandit gangs, reveal a common method: terrorise civilians, spread fear and force the state and society into submission. This is a structural resemblance showing that these jihadist groups are guided by the same ideological principles. Ansaru emerged from Boko Haram, while ISWAP is a separate jihadist faction that allied with Boko Haram factions. It is so unfortunate that such groups have been flowering in the North over the past 17 years. The authorities must investigate operational links, shared logistics, weapons, financing and local collaborators rather than blur distinctions. The assassination follows a recent disturbing viral video from Zamfara in which a young man and other youths reportedly called for AK-47s to attack Christian worshippers in Enugu and Jos. The police took the suspect into custody. Such threats, like Ansaru’s, expose the danger posed by violent preaching and impunity. Religious organisations must discipline inciters, while government must investigate and prosecute identified threats. Singapore, a multireligious country, uses its Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act to restrain religious leaders who incite hostility and punish advocacy of religious violence, with review safeguards. Nigeria should strengthen comparable, constitutionally protected enforcement, monitor credible threats, protect threatened clerics and prosecute financiers and gunmen. business.title: Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide Amundi, Europe’s largest asset manager, raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by about 44% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 6 shows, lifting the position to 1,903,725 shares worth $291.4 million at Sept. 30 prices. That is up 579,672 shares from the 1,324,053 Amundi reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $115.1 million. The Paris-based firm managed €2.579 trillion in assets at the end of September, up 11% year over year, and described itself as Europe’s leading asset manager. The filing lands as MSTR has given back much of its third-quarter run. Strategy shares closed at $153.09 on Sept. 30 and near $126 on Monday, an 18% drop that would put Amundi’s disclosed stake near $239 million at the latest close, Yahoo Finance data show. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. Amundi filed a combination report that folds in 17 other managers across its group, so the Strategy line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. Strategy keeps buying while the stock slides Strategy itself kept stacking. The company bought another 1,036 bitcoin last week for $81.9 million at an average of $79,012, a Monday 8-K filing and company release show, lifting its treasury to 850,364 BTC acquired for $64.16 billion at an average of $75,456. That average cost now sits above the spot bitcoin price, leaving the stack underwater on paper even after the firm added 811 bitcoin the prior week. Strategy’s public ledger still ranks it as the largest corporate bitcoin holder, with the stack equal to roughly 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. MSTR roughly doubled during the third quarter itself. The June 30 13F valued Amundi’s then-smaller stake at an implied $86.93 a share, against the $153.09 Sept. 30 close, so the dollar value of the position rose faster than the share count. Since then the stock has tracked bitcoin’s slide into the mid-$70,000s, wiping out a large share of that mark-to-market gain for anyone still holding the Sept. 30 position. The timing matters because Strategy funds most of its bitcoin buys by selling new MSTR common under an at-the-market program. A weaker share price raises more dilution for every coin purchased, which is the feedback loop that has defined the stock’s moves this year. Banks loaded bitcoin proxies in the same quarter Amundi was not the only large European name adding bitcoin exposure on the quarter. Barclays’ own 13F, also filed Nov. 6, shows 3,942,900 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) worth $186.7 million at Sept. 30, up 48% from 2,658,147 shares three months earlier, SEC records show. Warren intends to use the committee’s investigative powers for oversight of prediction markets and election betting platforms, aimed at insider trading and platform manipulation — the same fight she opened before the midterms. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. But they taught me that most people do not have a money problem. They have a decision problem. We are a generation that earns, spends, plans and postpones, often all at the same time. You can earn a lot and still not be wealthy One idea I keep returning to is that you can earn twenty million naira a year and still not be wealthy. Income is what comes in. Wealth is what stays and grows. Two people can earn the same salary and end up in completely different places ten years later, simply because one converted part of that income into assets and the other converted all of it into lifestyle. Wealthy people do not always look wealthy. Some of the most financially secure people I have met do not drive the loudest cars. And some of the people who look the richest are one bad month away from panic. So the question I now ask myself, and the people I speak with, is simple: what exactly are you converting your income into? entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. sports.title: ‘Didn’t know much about him’: DeMarcus Cousins says his favourite Lakers player is not Luka Doncic
sports.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images Luka Doncic is the biggest star in the Los Angeles Lakers’ locker room. The Slovenian is one of the best in the business, and if he continues at the same rate, he will likely win the MVP award this season. That is why Doncic is almost everybody’s favourite Lakers player, but DeMarcus Cousins’ pick is actually someone else. DeMarcus Cousins says Walker Kessler is his favourite Lakers player Walker Kessler joined the Los Angeles Lakers in July via a sign-and-trade deal on a four-year, $130 million contract. The 25-year-old had made a terrific name for himself while playing for the Utah Jazz, and his game has gone up a level since moving to LA. Kessler usually starts at centre alongside Doncic, and even though it’s the latter who makes all the headlines, the former has mostly been incredible as well. Cousins has watched a lot of the Lakers this season, and he has named Kessler as his favourite player ahead of the likes of Doncic and Austin Reaves. He said on the Run The Ball show: “My favourite player in this team is Walker Kessler. “I didn’t know much about him in Utah, but the way he controls the paint and the way he protects the rim… He had a few incredible blocks against Ausar Thompson, who is a freak athlete.” Cousins then had his say on the Lakers, a team he had made fun of before the start of the season. He has now held his hands up and admitted that they deserve respect. He said: “This is a pretty well-rounded team. Early on, there were a lot of jokes. I was one of the main people joking. It didn’t quite look great on paper. But seeing how this team is starting to shape up, you’ve got to put some respect on this Lakers group and the guys on this team. “Reaves is playing at an All-Star level right now. He put on an incredible performance. I love everything I’m seeing from this Lakers team right now.” The Lakers really are looking good, and everyone on the team, like Kessler, is producing the goods on a consistent basis. That, combined with Doncic playing out of his skin and looking like the next MVP, gives the Los Angeles side a great chance of going all the way this season. sports.title: Arsenal have already blown their WSL title chances - but Gunners still have the talent to win another Women's Champions League

Even at this early stage, their hopes of lifting a first WSL title since 2019 look doomed. Yet, as strange as it may seem given their struggles, that does not mean they should be overlooked in the Champions League. It's not been smooth-sailing in the early knockings of their European adventure by any means. A narrow 1-0 win over HB Koge in their first outing was a real struggle, with the Danes unlucky not to get anything from a game won by Mariona Caldentey's stoppage-time penalty . Then came an eventful 2-2 draw away at Paris FC, where an inexplicable handball by Leah Williamson allowed the hosts to complete their comeback from 2-0 down . At the time, there was a feeling that could be the final game for head coach Renee Slegers. But the Dutchwoman remains at the helm as the Gunners prepare for a huge couple of weeks in this competition having overseen a much more convincing 3-0 win over Benfica in the team's last European outing. Now, two huge tests beckon: away at Barcelona, the reigning champions , on Thursday before the hosting of eight-time winners Lyon a week later. It's a great chance for Arsenal, winners of this competition just 18 months ago , to remind everyone what they are capable of. The Gunners have regularly looked out of ideas, defensively weak and unable to maximise the talent in this squad, which was massively increased by what looked, on paper, like an outstanding transfer window . But it is worth noting that Arsenal have a history of starting seasons slowly. Regrets were traced back to September and October, where draws against Manchester United and Aston Villa proved costly before a defeat to City. sports.title: What made Youri Tielemans’ first Man United strike unique in Premier League era
sports.description: What made Youri Tielemans’ first Man United strike unique in Premier League era Manchester United’s Youri Tielemans opened his account for the Red Devils at the weekend. Goalscoring The Belgian is not renowned for scoring large numbers of goals, but when he does, they are usually spectacular or important. Or both, as in the Europa League final last season for Aston Villa against Freiburg. Tielemans scored just ten times for his former club in 134 matches. In addition, he added only 28 strikes in 195 games for Leicester City, but one of them was the winning goal in the 2021 FA Cup final. Man United goal Tielemans thought he had opened his account last month against Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford, but the goal was ruled out. Nonetheless, he finally got on the scoresheet during his 14th match for the club, having been an ever-present so far this season. The Belgian midfielder pulled his side level at 2-2 just before half time against Aston Villa when Zion Suzuki could not keep out the effort. His muted celebrations were out of respect for his former team, even though he must have been delighted to open his account in front of the Stretford End in such dramatic circumstances. The club’s official website has also reported on why the goal was special. The site reports, “it’s taken pretty extensive research but, by our reckoning, no United man has ever scored his first Premier League goal for the club against a former side.” Teddy Sheringham also almost did in August 1997 against Tottenham Hotspur, but his penalty cannoned off the post and out. Ralph Milne did achieve this in 1988 when he scored his first United goal against his former side Charlton Athletic. Tommy Boyle also scored in 1929 against his former side Sheffield United, and George Livingston in 1909 against his old team, Manchester City.

sports.title: All quiet on extension front as Sal Stewart's value rises with award
sports.description: LAS VEGAS – Sal Stewart’s Rookie of the Year award brought good news and bad news for the Cincinnati Reds this week. The good news is that thanks to new rules in the game meant to disincentivize service-time manipulation the Reds get an additional draft pick between the first and second rounds. The not-so-good news: The price just went up on the inevitable extension talks with the hard-hitting, 22-year-old All-Star. Reds GM meetings 4 great free agent fits for Cincinnati Reds as MLB's GM meetings open Four months after the Reds inked Stewart’s pal, Reds ace Chase Burns, to a $105 million, seven-year extension, the Reds and Stewart still had not engaged in talks about an extension for the 32-homer rookie slugger, sources said. And the meter continues to run after Stewart became the franchise’s ninth player to win the National League Rookie of the Year award, with Stewart also a finalist for a prestigious Silver Slugger award. Those winners are announced next week. The tangible upside for the team — beyond possibly earning a few more ticket sales in marketing the “award-winning” Sal — is the Prospect Promotion Incentive draft pick that figures to be a top-40 overall pick between their first- and second-round picks. That’s because of a 2022 rule that rewards teams for promoting prospects closer to the beginning of a season rather than wait long enough with their better prospects to assure an additional year of club control before free agency. That delay of less than two weeks led to players such as Kris Bryant and Maikel Franco to file union grievances a decade ago against their teams for service-time manipulation that delayed their free agency. Bryant won a Rookie of the Year award in 2015 after being kept in the minors the first eight games of that season, which meant an additional six years before he was eligible for free agency. How potentially valuable are the additional supplemental picks? Stewart was selected 32nd overall in 2022 – as an additional compensation pick for the Reds for losing Nick Castellanos as a free agent. sports.title: 'Leicester draw is game for the fans and for Dover'
sports.description: Dover manager Jake Leberl said the club would embrace the occasion [BBC] The manager of non-league Dover Athletic says the club's FA Cup draw against former Premier League champions Leicester City is "a game for the fans and for the town". Manager Jake Leberl described it as an "unbelievable draw". "[I'm] so pleased for everyone - the chairman who's been here so many years pumping money in, the new investors, and the fans who've had it hard for quite a few years," he said. Chairman of the sixth division side, Jim Parmenter, told BBC Radio Kent : "This is just one off in every 10 years." Leberl said his first thought was: "I would love to get to the third round." He said that would be "incredibly hard", adding: "But what a day and obviously financially brilliant for the club." The second round match between Dover and the 2021 FA Cup champions will take place on the weekend starting 4 December. The match against the League One side has drawn comparisons to Dover's 2015 FA Cup tie at home against Crystal Palace, who won 4-0 . Leberl, who was assistant manager at the time, said: "Football-wise [it is an] incredibly difficult game, but it's a game for the fans and for the town and we'll just embrace it and do the best we can." Parmenter said it would be "a fantastic day" for all the supporters. "But particularly [it is] a reward for all the volunteers, the hard working staff we've got here that have stuck with the club all through the tough times, the downs, the Covid situation, the points deductions, the fines, everything else," he added. Leicester City won the FA Cup in 2021 [Getty Images] In the FA Cup, second round winners receive £79,500 in prize money, while £21,200 is given to the losing side. The chairman said he hoped the money would act as a "platform for us to move the club forward". "It's a cup game, it's 90 minutes of football, our squad's right on top of their game at the moment, we're scoring goals, we're defending well, so why shouldn't we have a go and try to win the tie?" he added. 'Everything is possible' Fan Lynne Lister, who was at the club to watch the draw, agreed with the chairman. "The atmosphere in here tonight tells you how pleased we are with our draw," she added. "Everything is possible." Fellow fan Jamie Skeggs said it was a "dream tie" for the club. "The players have put in so much hard work and they deserve this, the fans deserve this after all the financial troubles we've had over the years," he added. "They may be ex-Premier League champions but they're coming to Crabble on a non-league pitch, they're not going to like it, so we'll see what happens." technology.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
technology.description: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. The product has become particularly useful since Anthropic's Mythos model, and similar AI offerings, made it possible to quickly find more software bugs and flaws and overwhelmed tech teams whose patching apparatus was not set up to handle hundreds of montly CVEs. Live Protect currently works on some of Cisco's datacenter switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. "Expect this to be a major investment area," Schultz added. ®

science.title: Global carbon emissions set to fall in 2026 due to Iran energy shock
science.description: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz led to a spike in oil prices Anna Ivanova/Alamy Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop this year for the first time in five years. The slowdown has been partly attributed to the energy shock triggered by the US and Israel’s war on Iran. The conflict, which began in February, led to a jump in oil prices after the Strait of Hormuz, the main trade route for about 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas, was blockaded by Iran in response. This is still affecting petrol prices and household gas bills, and has seen countries around the world turn to alternative fuel types to boost energy security. Advertisement Read more Solar energy is going to power the world much sooner than you think Around 38.2 gigatonnes of CO2 are expected to be emitted in 2026 globally, according to the latest annual Global Carbon Budget – put together by more than 140 researchers. This is a 0.4 per cent decrease on the previous year, largely due to a projected 1.9 per cent fall in emissions from oil. The drop in oil use was partly offset by a 0.6 per cent increase in emissions from coal. Robbie Andrew at climate research group CICERO in Oslo, Norway, one of the report authors, says financial pressures due to the energy shock are likely to have caused the drop in emissions this year, which may turn out to be a “blip”. “On the assumption that there are no further crises, then you’d expect that emissions would bounce back,” says Andrew. The two biggest dips in emissions in the 21st century have been attributed to the covid-19 pandemic, which saw emissions drop by around 6 per cent in 2020, and the global financial crisis, which saw emissions drop around 2 per cent in 2009. The future outlook depends on how long the energy shock lasts, says Andrew, with governments forced to look at the economic case for continuing to subsidise fossil fuels. The rollout of renewable energy also played a part in bringing down carbon emissions. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power are predicted to offset 64 to 79 per cent of increasing emissions from demand growth through to 2028. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter In China, the world’s biggest emitter of CO2, emissions are projected to decrease by 0.9 per cent in 2026 as the country continues to make strides with expanding renewable energy and electric vehicles. “What’s keeping emissions down is the renewable energy, and the price of oil actually suppresses this even more,” says Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia, UK, who also worked on the report. “So, that’s encouraging in a way, but it does mean that if the price of oil rebounds to pre-Iran [conflict] levels, most likely the emissions will rebound as well until we have enough further acceleration in renewable energy to really bring the emissions down durably.” Journal Reference: Nature Climate Change DOI: 10.1038/s41558-026-02821-8

Perseverance is equipped with a fantastic set of instruments for studying the rock record of this ancient planet. Both PIXL and SuperCam have great capabilities for detecting all kinds of elements. SHERLOC, SuperCam, and PIXL can detect minerals using various techniques including x-ray fluorescence, Raman, and infrared spectroscopies. As a side benefit of the way SuperCam performs its Raman spectroscopy, it can also study time-resolved luminescence. Normally luminescence occurs over a broad wavelength range (most of Earth’s commercial lighting uses luminescence in some way or another). Two years ago, the SuperCam team was startled to find strong, narrow luminescence peaks at two wavelengths of 692.7 and 694.1 nanometers when they shot a light-colored rock with the laser. This luminescence comes from delayed atomic transitions in chromium atoms present in a corundum mineral structure. SuperCam can time the delay of the atomic transitions via the resulting photons, and so we could verify that this emission came from chromium in corundum. The results were published in Geophysical Research Letters by a team led by Ann Ollila earlier this year, so you can read all about it. The gemstone version of chromium-containing corundum is ruby. Prior to installing SuperCam on Perseverance, we placed a ruby in the laser beam and watched the entire room pulse a brilliant red as SuperCam’s laser beam hit the gemstone; it was extremely bright. While we haven’t found collectable rubies on Mars yet, the little corundum crystals are helping us learn more about Mars’ past. Corundum is a metamorphic and pegmatitic mineral which we would not expect to find on Mars, a planet that lacks plate tectonics. However, large meteor and asteroid impacts can create local metamorphism due to long-term heating from the impact. Because we are in a very ancient terrain near the rim of Jezero crater, we can expect some evidence of localized metamorphism. As the first mission in such terrain, we are learning new things. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
science.description: null On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes. The rocket carried an uncrewed command module that splashed down in the Pacific Ocean. NASA's first-ever Saturn V rocket launches on its maiden flight from Cape Canaveral, Florida on the uncrewed Apollo 4 test flight on Nov. 9, 1967. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered The launch of Apollo 4 in November 1967 was a turning point for NASA on its path to landing astronauts on the moon. The space agency had bet the moon on its new Saturn V booster, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to fly astronauts in a capsule (as well as their lander) to the moon and back. But the rocket had never been fully tested until the Apollo 4 launch. NASA also needed a new launch site for its Apollo missions. So the agency built Launch Complex 39 at what is now called the Kennedy Space Center, a Florida spaceport that has become the home port for orbital human spaceflight in the United States. But in 1967, no rockets had ever flown from the site. Yet, everything went according to plan. The launch came as NASA was on its heels. Just months earlier, on Jan. 27, 1967, the space agency suffered a fatal tragedy when Apollo 1 astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee died on the launch pad after a fire broke out inside their Apollo command module during a ground test. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. science.description: A composite NASA Chandra X-ray and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optical image of the galaxy NGC 4559 located about 30 million light-years from Earth. The Chandra data shows X-ray point sources represented in purple, and the SDSS data shows the galaxy and foreground and background objects in red and blue. Aghakhanloo et al.; Optical: SDSS; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study , published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. Eta Carinae, for example, is a particularly well-known luminous blue variable.) AT 2016blu is a special type of luminous blue variable that undergoes rapid and repeated increases in brightness. science.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
science.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . "An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable." The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain. "The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said.
